question_text: Specify an aging temperature for a $95 \mathrm{Al}-5 \mathrm{Cu}$ alloy that will produce a maximum of $5 \mathrm{wt} \% \theta$ precipitate. Give your answer as the value of aging_temperature.The unit of the answer is °C.
response:
## Solution

**Step 1 — Lever rule setup**

For the 95Al-5Cu alloy (C₀ = 5 wt% Cu), the equilibrium fraction of θ (Al₂Cu, Cθ ≈ 53 wt% Cu) at an aging temperature is:

$$f_\theta = \frac{C_0 - C_\alpha}{C_\theta - C_\alpha}$$

**Step 2 — Solve for required matrix composition**

Setting f_θ = 0.05 (the maximum allowed 5 wt% θ):

$$C_\alpha = \frac{C_0 - f_\theta C_\theta}{1 - f_\theta} = \frac{5 - 0.05(53)}{0.95} = \frac{2.35}{0.95} \approx 2.47 \text{ wt% Cu}$$

**Step 3 — Find the temperature on the solvus where Cu solubility in α-Al equals 2.47 wt%**

The Al-rich solvus of the Al-Cu diagram passes through ~5.65 wt% at 548 °C (eutectic) and decreases with temperature. Reading/interpolating the solvus (both linear and Arrhenius interpolation between the 450 °C / 2.5 wt% and 475 °C / 3.2 wt% data points) gives the temperature where solubility = 2.47 wt% Cu:

$$T \approx 449\text{–}452\ °C \;\approx\; 450\ °C$$

Aging below ~450 °C would drive the equilibrium θ fraction above 5 wt%; aging above it keeps θ below 5 wt%. Thus the highest permissible aging temperature (giving exactly the 5 wt% maximum) is:

$$\boxed{450}$$
